touches.text: A device talks to other devices only over the bus, never by importing them.

Owns the Claude Code hooks: mail check, the turn-shape and ask scans, the gates on record writes and deletes. Anything that adapts CC specifically to Cairn goes in the CC device, and every one of CC's scripts lives here.
bus_client: gets a process onto the bus (reach a device, or connect). Its connect is a wake attempt (5.3.5.1). USERS: every process that speaks.

The RULE 1 check is a path check: code inside device bar may not import cairn.devices.foo (anything not under cairn.devices.bar), except a tool foo publishes (cairn.devices.foo.tools.<x>, its charter saying published_by_device). Inside one device there is one owner, so nothing is checked there. A charter's public_interface describes what the component offers (modules, functions, bus verbs, commands); the check does not read it. Akien 2026-11-09 (Q#77): "wouldn't it be easier (for the python code anyway) to see if the imports do not include other device paths?"
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.

conflicts.text: VERBS: crossing, watch. COMMANDS: cairn codemother harbor_master -> "652 boats (570 open, 82 in port)".
conflicts.ticket_says: cross.py calls harbor_master with verb='clear' via bus.request(...verb='clear'...). D1 references '_handle_clear' in harbor_master/device.py, and falsifier clause 2 specifies the crossing is exactly one request to harbor_master with verb clear.
conflicts.why: The outline at 9.4.1.5 explicitly lists harbor_master's verbs as only 'crossing, watch.' The ticket requires a 'clear' verb not in this list. Either the outline is wrong about which verbs exist, or the ticket cannot work because it calls a verb the design does not define. Both cannot stand unless the outline is updated.
